summary: Master Construction Claims, Delay Analysis & Dispute Management in 5 days. Learn EOT calculation, forensic schedule analysis, and dispute resolution.
lede: Construction claims management training equips intermediate construction contract, scheduling and commercial professionals to assess delay-related entitlement and prepare supported claims. Learners build and review CPM schedules, calculate extensions of time using Time Impact Analysis, assemble evidence and quantify loss and expense, and practise negotiation or mediation for disputed claims.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate-level professionals who must secure project income, mitigate financial risk, and resolve disputes before they escalate to arbitration. It is ideal for those with 2-5 years of experience in construction contracts, scheduling, or commercial management. By the end of this course, you will be able to lead claims preparation, perform forensic delay analysis, and resolve disputes through negotiation or mediation. This course is designed for: Contract Administrator:
audience: Manage FIDIC/NEC4 contract compliance and submit EOT
Project Manager: Oversee project schedules and resolve
Claims Specialist: Prepare and substantiate loss
Commercial Manager: Quantify financial impact of delays
Construction Lawyer: Advise on contractual entitlements
Site Engineer: Document contemporary records and identify
Dispute Resolution Advisor: Facilitate mediation and prepare
Cost Engineer: Calculate productivity loss and overheads
Project Controls Manager: Monitor schedule performance
Risk Manager: Assess delay risks and implement
modules: Foundations of Construction Claims and Contractual Entitlement
Project Scheduling and Critical Path Analysis Fundamentals
Delay Analysis Methods and EOT Calculation
Dispute Resolution Strategies and Negotiation Techniques
Forensic Delay Analysis and Complex Dispute Scenarios
Dispute Management Strategy and Stakeholder Communication
Digital Transformation and AI in Delay Analysis
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of construction contracts (FIDIC or NEC4) and basic project scheduling concepts (Critical Path Method). No coding or advanced software skills required. Equipment: Bring a laptop with MS Project or Primavera P6 installed (cloud version provided if needed). Pre-course: Recommended reading on FIDIC/NEC4 contract clauses (provided in digital pack).
